observed_behavior: The same implementation snapshot produced three strict-clean observed 50k/5k benchmark passes, then BDD-016 repeated real wall-clock measurement and returned MIXED_OPERATION_EVIDENCE/inconclusive with an unchanged functional digest.
expected_behavior: The full-scale owner BDD must deterministically verify functional, schema, producer, cleanup, three-sample, and four-state classification contracts with controlled timing evidence; only three predeclared strict-clean standalone observed commands decide delivery performance, and any non-pass is retained and stops without retry-until-green.
impact: A correct snapshot can pass all dedicated performance gates and then be blocked by a duplicate host-timing window inside the owner suite, so delivery cannot simultaneously satisfy deterministic baseline and fail-closed completion requirements.

reproduction.symptom_oracle: At the same implementation SHA, fixture shape, and functional digest, the three dedicated observed reports pass while a later BDD-016 observed timing window returns a non-pass.
steps: From a strict-clean worktree, run each of the three predeclared standalone 50k/5k observed benchmark commands once and retain every report.
Compare BDD-016 measurement mode, functional_sha256, raw timing samples, classification, report verdict, cleanup, and exit code against the dedicated reports.
reproduction.sample: Three retained standalone reports passed with maximum samples 1.1978953999932855s, 1.6081831000046805s, and 1.45902730000671s. Seq99 then had cold_query_1 breaches 2/3, cold_query_2 breaches 1/3, fixture setup 49.119367600011174s, matching functional SHA, and verdict inconclusive.

root_cause.summary: Evidence supports duplicated observed wall-clock responsibility as the contract-level cause of conflicting completion verdicts; the underlying seq99 latency source remains unconfirmed among traversal state, fixture sequence, and external Windows load.

hypotheses.statement: Owner BDD and standalone commands both make performance decisions from uncontrolled observed wall-clock windows, allowing valid timing variance to produce conflicting completion verdicts for one snapshot.
hypotheses.variable: BDD-016 timing evidence mode while fixture, functional path, sample count, and classifier stay fixed.
hypotheses.prediction: Controlled BDD sequences are repeatable while standalone observed gates still fail closed for real sustained violations.
hypotheses.falsifier: Controlled BDD still changes with host duration, or standalone observed gates can no longer detect sustained violations.

hypotheses.statement: Fresh-fixture cache or filesystem state makes the 5,000-page traversal or cold query intermittently slow under a specific predecessor sequence.
hypotheses.variable: BDD predecessor sequence or fresh-versus-reused fixture state.
hypotheses.prediction: Breaches cluster reproducibly under one sequence or fixture state.
hypotheses.falsifier: Repeated samples show no sequence correlation, or isolated runs retain the same distribution.

hypotheses.statement: External Windows CPU, filesystem-filter, or process pressure is the main source of the seq99 latency window.
hypotheses.variable: Measured host resource pressure while repository inputs remain fixed.
hypotheses.prediction: Outlier frequency rises with external pressure and returns to baseline after pressure is removed.
hypotheses.falsifier: An isolated low-load run deterministically toggles the failure through one internal product variable.

next_action: Bind assessment revision 3 and Requirements v4 under one exact approval, then produce a new Ready Plan for a minimal controlled BDD timing seam, explicit measurement-mode contract, generation 2 handoff, and fixed stop-on-first-non-pass verification sequence.
